'''Greta Cvetanova Panova'''<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=153500}}.</ref> ({{langx|bg|Грета Цветанова Панова}}, born 1983 in [[Sofia|Sofia, Bulgaria]]) is a [[Bulgarian-American]] [[mathematician]]. She is a professor of mathematics and Gabilan Distinguished Professor in Science and Engineering at the [[University of Southern California]] in [[Los Angeles]].  Her research interests include [[combinatorics]], [[probability]] and [[theoretical computer science]].

==Education and career==
Panova received her B.S. in 2005 from [[MIT]]. She received M.A. in 2006 from [[University of California, Berkeley]] and Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] in 2011, under the supervision of [[Richard P. Stanley]].  She was then a postdoc at [[UCLA]] (2011–2014), Assistant and Associate Professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] (2014–2018), and is currently a tenured Professor at the [[University of Southern California]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://uscdornsife.usc.edu/tools/mytools/PersonnelInfoSystem/DOC/Faculty/MATH/vita_1085762.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae: Greta C. Panova|publisher=USC|date=October 7, 2023|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref> In 2023, she was named Gabilan Distinguished Professor.<ref>{{citation|url=https://wise.usc.edu/programs/grants-and-awards/faculty/galiban-distinguished-professorship-in-science-and-engineering/|access-date=June 4, 2024|title=Gabilan Distinguished Professorship in Science and Engineering|publisher=USC}}</ref>

Panova research is in [[algebraic combinatorics]] with applications to [[geometric complexity theory]], probability and [[statistical mechanics]].<ref name=birman />  {{As of|2024}}, she is a co-Editor-in-Chief of the ''[[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]]'', and a member of the editorial board of [[Algebraic Combinatorics (journal)|''Algebraic Combinatorics'']] and the ''[[Arnold Mathematical Journal]]''.<ref>[https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/about/editorialTeam Editorial team], ''[[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]]''.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/|title=Arnold Mathematical Journal|publisher=Stony Brook University|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://alco.centre-mersenne.org/page/editorial-board/|title=Editorial Team|publisher=Centre Mersenne|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref>

==Selected awards==
Panova was a three time medalist at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (1999–2001, one gold and two silver medals) and a third prize winner at the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]] (2001).<ref>[https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=5541 Greta Panova stats] on the official IMO website.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://kskedlaya.org/putnam-archive/putnam2001results.html|title=Announcement of winners of the sixty-second competition held on December 1, 2001|author=Kiran Kedlaya|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref>  She is a recipient of Katz Fellowship (UC Berkeley), Putnam Fellowship (Harvard), James Mills Peirce Fellowship (Harvard), [[Simons Foundation|Simons Postdoctoral Fellowship]] (UCLA), and von Neumann Fellowship ([[Institute for Advanced Study|IAS]]).<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/scholars/greta-panova Greta Panova profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013230613/https://www.ias.edu/scholars/greta-panova |date=2019-10-13 }} as von Neumann Fellow, [[Institute for Advanced Study]].</ref> Panova was an invited plenary speaker at the 2017 [[International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics]] and at the 2023 [[Current Developments in Mathematics Conference]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://fpsac.org/invited_speakers/|title=All time invited speakers|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Current Developments in Mathematics Conference 2023|url=https://cmsa.fas.harvard.edu/event/cdm-2023/|publisher=Harvard University|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref> Panova is the 2020 recipient of the IMI Award, awarded once every three years by the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics at the [[Bulgarian Academy of Science]] to a Bulgarian citizen under the age of 40 for high achievements in the field of mathematics,<ref>{{citation|url=https://math.bas.bg/imi-award/?lang=en|title=IMI Mathematics Prize|publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref> and the 2024–5 Birman Fellow of the [[American Mathematics Society]].<ref name=birman>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7271|title=Panova Awarded 2024-2025 Birman Fellowship|date=December 20, 2023|publisher=AMS|access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref>
